projects.name: MediaStorm
projects.description: Independent streaming media server with its own backend and first-party mobile/TV apps, focused on Debrid and Usenet streaming.

aiostreams.note: AIOStreams is explicitly listed as a supported scraper and has a dedicated backend scraper implementation.

evidence.claim: The official README lists AIOStreams under supported scraping sources.
The backend contains a dedicated AIOStreams scraper implementation.

apple_tv.note: First-party tvOS app is distributed through TestFlight.

evidence.claim: The official README documents a tvOS TestFlight build.

android_tv.note: First-party Android TV APK is publicly linked from the README.

evidence.claim: The official README links an Android TV APK and release history.

web.note: An admin web UI is documented; a first-party browser playback client was not separately verified.

evidence.claim: The README describes MediaStorm as a streaming media server that requires both backend and frontend, with Debrid and Usenet support.

projects.name: Remux
projects.description: Independent Rust media server exposing a Jellyfin-compatible API and combining Stremio add-ons, local files, WebDAV, and torrent sources.

aiostreams.note: Remux implements a generic Stremio-addon preset; its source explicitly says the preset includes AIO rather than implementing a separate AIOStreams-only provider.

evidence.claim: The Stremio preset accepts any addon speaking the Stremio addon protocol and explicitly says it includes AIO.

apple_tv.note: Remux documents Infuse as a compatible Jellyfin client; Infuse is available on Apple TV.

evidence.claim: The Remux README lists Infuse among compatible Jellyfin clients.
Firecore documents Infuse support for Apple TV/tvOS.

android_tv.note: The README names Jellyfin for Android but Android TV coverage was not separately verified for this record.

web.note: Jellyfin-compatible client coverage is broad, but browser playback compatibility was not separately verified for this record.

evidence.claim: The README describes Remux as a self-hosted Jellyfin-compatible media server with Stremio add-ons, local files, WebDAV, and torrents.

projects.name: Fetcherr
projects.description: Jellyfin-compatible streaming bridge for clients such as Infuse and VidHub, resolving playback through Debrid streams returned by Stremio add-ons.

aiostreams.note: AIOStreams is explicitly documented as a supported Stremio add-on provider, including setup guidance and direct-playable-URL handling.

evidence.claim: The official README requires a playable Stremio add-on and names AIOStreams, then documents AIOStreams-specific setup and playback behavior.

apple_tv.note: Fetcherr explicitly targets Infuse; Infuse is available on Apple TV.

evidence.claim: The official README describes Fetcherr as a Jellyfin-compatible streaming bridge for Infuse and documents connecting Infuse.
Firecore documents Infuse support for Apple TV/tvOS.

android_tv.note: No Android TV client path was verified for this record.

web.note: Fetcherr has web setup/settings UI, but browser playback was not verified as a first-party client path.

evidence.claim: The README describes Jellyfin-compatible search/playback, Real-Debrid or TorBox resolution, and Infuse/VidHub client paths.

projects.name: Hound
projects.description: Independent hybrid media server combining a traditional self-hosted library with instant P2P, Debrid, Usenet, and IPTV streaming.

aiostreams.note: The official README explicitly names AIOStreams for P2P, HTTP/Debrid, and Usenet streaming through Stremio add-ons.

evidence.claim: The Hound README explicitly says content can be streamed from P2P, HTTP/Debrid sources and Usenet through Stremio addons (AIOStreams).

apple_tv.note: Hound says iOS/tvOS share a codebase and can currently be run through Xcode, but are not yet publicly distributed.

evidence.claim: The official README says iOS and tvOS are not available yet and can currently only be run through Xcode.

android_tv.note: Android TV APKs are published through the Hound app repository releases.

evidence.claim: The official README directs users to downloadable Android and Android TV apps in the app repository releases.

web.note: Hound includes and documents its own web frontend and public demo.

evidence.claim: The README documents a web frontend, development server, and public demo.
The README describes Hound as a fully featured hybrid media server with local media, P2P, HTTP/Debrid, and Usenet streaming.

projects.name: Riven RS
projects.description: Independent community Rust implementation of Riven that automates discovery/resolution and exposes stream-aware media through a FUSE VFS to external media servers.

aiostreams.note: Riven RS contains a built-in AIOStreams source plugin with its own settings and documentation.

evidence.claim: The official plugin documentation describes an AIOStreams scraper that queries a configured AIOStreams instance.
The Riven RS README lists AIOStreams among built-in torrent scraper plugins.

apple_tv.note: Playback is delegated to the external media server; Apple TV support depends on that chosen media-server/client stack.

android_tv.note: Playback is delegated to the external media server; Android TV support depends on that chosen media-server/client stack.

web.note: Riven has its own management frontend, while media playback is delegated to an external media server.

evidence.claim: The README describes FUSE output for Jellyfin, Emby, Plex, or other media servers and built-in plugins for Debrid and Usenet.

projects.name: Riven TS
projects.description: Official Riven rewrite: self-hosted media automation using Debrid, StremThru, a FUSE VFS, and external Plex or Jellyfin media servers.

aiostreams.note: Current official documentation names Torrentio and Comet for scraping and StremThru for Debrid. No current first-party AIOStreams integration was confirmed during this review.

apple_tv.note: Playback is delegated to Plex or Jellyfin; Apple TV support depends on the selected downstream media-server/client stack.

android_tv.note: Playback is delegated to Plex or Jellyfin; Android TV support depends on the selected downstream media-server/client stack.

web.note: Riven exposes management APIs/UI, while playback is delegated to the media server.

evidence.claim: Official Riven TS documentation describes the pipeline as Torrentio/Comet to StremThru/Debrid to FUSE VFS to Plex or Jellyfin.

projects.name: Silo
projects.description: Independent self-hosted media server for operator-controlled on-disk libraries, with a built-in web app and Jellyfin/Emby-compatible API.

aiostreams.note: AIOStreams is not named in the non-goals document, but an AIOStreams-style remote-stream integration conflicts with Silo's documented permanent exclusion of remote URL shortcut/fetch/proxy/redirect/transcode capabilities in core, plugins, and clients.

evidence.claim: Silo's permanent non-goals exclude .strm and equivalent remote media URL shortcuts, including fetching, proxying, redirecting or transcoding those streams, and state this is unavailable in core, plugins, or clients.

apple_tv.note: Silo explicitly lists Infuse as a Jellyfin/Emby-compatible client; Infuse is available on Apple TV.

evidence.claim: The Silo README lists Infuse among clients for its Jellyfin/Emby-compatible API.
Firecore documents Infuse support for Apple TV/tvOS.

android_tv.note: The README names compatible clients, but Android TV coverage was not separately verified for this record.

web.note: Silo includes its own web app.

evidence.claim: The official README explicitly says to use the included web app or the Jellyfin/Emby-compatible API.
The README describes Silo as a self-hosted media server for on-disk media with an included web app and Jellyfin/Emby-compatible API.
The non-goals document says Silo indexes and plays media that exists on disk in an operator-controlled library and permanently excludes remote-stream shortcuts.
